Polygons and triangles

Source: R/matgeo-geometry-polygon.R
Polygon.Rd

Polygon() builds a polygon from its vertices as SymPy does: repeated and collinear vertices are removed, so that three vertices give a Triangle, two a segment and one a point; n gives a regular polygon. Triangle() also accepts sss, asa or sas (side lengths and angles in degrees). RegularPolygon() takes a center, a radius, the number of sides and a rotation. The vertices are in $vertices.

Usage

Polygon(..., n = 0)

Triangle(...)

RegularPolygon(c, r, n, rot = 0)

angles(p)

perimeter(p)

first_moment_of_area(p, point = NULL)

sides(p)

cut_section(p, line)

apothem(p)

interior_angle(p)

exterior_angle(p)

rotation(p)

spin(p, angle)

is_similar(t1, t2)

is_equilateral(t)

is_isosceles(t)

is_scalene(t)

is_right(t)

altitudes(t)

orthocenter(t)

circumcenter(t)

circumradius(t)

circumcircle(t)

incenter(t)

inradius(t)

incircle(t)

exradii(t)

excenters(t)

medians(t)

medial(t)

nine_point_circle(t)

eulerline(t)

Arguments

...

Vertices; for Triangle() also sss, asa or sas.

n

The number of sides of a regular polygon.

c, r

The center and radius of a regular polygon.

rot, angle

Rotation angles.

p, t, t1, t2

Polygons, triangles or other entities.

point

A reference point.

line

A line.

Value

An entity, an expression, a logical value or a list.

Details

The functions are SymPy's methods and properties: sides(), angles(), perimeter(), is_convex(), encloses(), cut_section(), first_moment_of_area(), the triangle centers circumcenter(), incenter(), orthocenter(), excenters() and the related circumradius(), circumcircle(), inradius(), incircle(), exradii(), altitudes(), medians(), medial(), nine_point_circle(), eulerline(), is_right(), is_equilateral(), is_isosceles(), is_scalene(), is_similar(), and for regular polygons apothem(), interior_angle(), exterior_angle(), rotation() and spin() (which returns the spun polygon). Results keyed by vertices or sides are named lists.

Examples

p <- Polygon(Point(0, 0), Point(1, 0), Point(1, 1), Point(0, 1))
area(p)
#> 1
perimeter(p)
#> 4
t <- Triangle(Point(0, 0), Point(4, 0), Point(0, 3))
circumcenter(t)
#> Point2D(2, 3/2) 
incenter(t)
#> Point2D(1, 1) 
Polygon(Point(0, 0), Point(1, 0), Point(2, 0), Point(1, 1))
#> Triangle(Point2D(0, 0), Point2D(2, 0), Point2D(1, 1))
